newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian airport signs 2.2 bln rgt bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian airport signs 2.2 bln rgt bond issue.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur International Airport Bhd, which is building a 9.0 billion ringgit airport south of the capital, on Saturday signed a 2.2 billion ringgit Islamic bond issue to help finance the project.
The issue will be in two tranches, officials said at a signing ceremony at the Malaysian Ministry of Finance.

The agreement, witnessed by Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim, involves a first tranche of 1.1 billion ringgit for five years and a second of 1.1 billion ringgit for seven years.
KLIA is owned by the Ministry of Finance.

Islamic bonds are zero coupon. The KLIA nonds are structured on the Al-Bai Bithaman Ajil (deferred payment sale) financing arrangement, similar to a sales and purchase agreement at predetermined prices, KLIA said in a statement.
Under Islam's Shariah principles, business should be done on the basis of sale and purchase of assets. Charging interest on loans is considered usury.
The religion forbids investing in traditional banks, gaming and liquor companies.
This is KLIA's second Islamic bonds issue to fund the airport, being built in Sepang, 70 km (44 miles) southwest of capital Kuala Lumpur.

In January last year, it issued 20-year bonds to raise 2.2 billion ringgit in what was then the biggest Islamic issue in the country. It was also the first Islamic paper to be traded in the local secondary market.
KLIA said then it had already raised 3.3 billion ringgit and needed to raise four billion more to fund the airport.
The bonds are part of Moslem Malaysia's efforts to promote the country as an Islamic financial centre, Anwar said.
"The KLIA's 2.2 billion ringgit bond is part of our efforts to become a centre for Islamic banking," he said in a speech at the signing ceremony.
"Islamic financial instruments should not just be an option but a viable alternative," he said.

Islamic instruments now accounted for 11.5 percent, or 4.8 billion ringgit, of the 42 billion ringgit in total outstanding private debt securities issued by the private sector as of December 31, 1996, Anwar said.
The total comprised 32 billion ringgit in corporate bonds and 10 billion in commercial paper, he said.
"In six years we have captured 11.5 percent. It shows the enormous potential for the Islamic financial system."

Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd has been appointed the facilitating agent for the issue. It is also the joint arranger along with DCB-Sakura Merchant Bankers Bhd, KAF Discounts Bhd and PhileoAllied Capital Bhd, the KLIA statement said.
The bonds will be issued on January 31, KLIA said.
It said the bonds have been guaranteed by the government and would carry a zero risk.
Islamic issues, for calculation purposes, carry an internal rate of return (IRR). The first KLIA bond is expected to be issued with an IRR of 7.6 percent, money dealers said.
In the secondary market, the bonds were last traded at an IRR of 7.35 percent, the dealers said.
They said the primary subscribers to the issue had sold the bonds to investors at an IRR of 7.25 percent.

"Several corporates and insurance companies took positions in the bond. But, when it was announced that it will not be a schedule one asset, people sold it," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
He said the yield went as low as 7.19, when the selling began and pulled up the IRR to 7.35 percent.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
($1=2.48 ringgit)
